newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police detain man in mystery arms case.
newsitem.headline: Indian police detain man in mystery arms case.

text.p: Indian immigration authorities have detained an American passport holder in connection with investigations into an air drop of arms near a West Bengal town just over a year ago, police said on Saturday.
The man, whose passport identifed him as Martin Konrad Schneider, 43, was held at Bombay's Sahar airport after he arrived from Singapore on Friday night, a police official told Reuters.

In December, 1995, Indian Air Force jets forced a Latvian cargo plane to land in Bombay as it tried to fly to Pakistan five days after a cache of sophisticated arms and ammunition was airdropped near the town of Purulia in West Bengal state.
Police arrested five Latvians and a Briton alleged to have been involved in the drop.
British arms dealer Peter Bleach pleaded not guilty to sedition and conspiracy charges when he went on trial in the eastern city of Calcutta last month.
The police official said the man held on Saturday could be an associate of a man known as Kim Davy, a prime suspect in the case who has not been traced.
Davy was the name on a forged New Zealand passport found by police when they searched the Latvian plane.
